title: Deep Learning Based Sinogram Inpainting for Fast and High-quality Artifact Correction in Electron Tomography
content: Reliable reconstruction from electron tomography (ET) of dense particles embedded in light support (e.g., Pt/C fuel cell catalyst) is a difficult problem. When the experiment is conducted in a coherent scattering mode, such as TEM or bright-field scanning TEM (BF-STEM), Bragg diffraction artifacts can introduce nonlinearities throughout the tilt series, complicating accurate reconstruction. Other inherent limitations of the technique are restricted tilt range and sparse sampling. These factors lead to artifacts—strong streaks and dark shades—in the reconstruction image, resulting in mischaracterization of the scanned sample. Traditional methods such as filtered back-projection (FBP) [1], or even superior algorithms like model-based iterative reconstruction (MBIR) [2], fail to provide reliable reconstruction in this case.
